meta.title: The Global Compute Supply Crisis | Infrastructure Scarcity
meta.description: Why GPU supply is only half the battle. The critical shortage of high-density power and data center halls worldwide.

hero.headline: Solving the Supply Side of the AI Equation
hero.subheadline: The world has the chips, but it lacks the 'plumbing'—the power and cooling needed to run them. We are building the plumbing in Kenya.

sections.title: The Invisible Bottleneck in AI Growth
sections.body: Mainstream media often focuses on the shortage of NVIDIA chips, but a more permanent and structural shortage is emerging: the shortage of high-density data center capacity. Standard data centers, built for web hosting and enterprise database storage, are not equipped to handle the 40kW-100kW per rack power requirements of modern AI clusters. Major tech hubs like Northern Virginia, Dublin, and Singapore have reached the limits of their electrical grids, leading to a freeze on new data center permits. This 'Gridlock' is our greatest opportunity. Kenya AI Compute circumvents the supply crisis by building vertically integrated capacity where power is abundant and industrial space is ready. We are providing the 'Critical Compute Real Estate' that the world's AI models are desperately searching for.

sections.title: The Supply Crisis Factors
items: Grid Saturation: Traditional tech capitals can no longer support high-density power growth.
Legacy Infrastructure: 80% of existing data centers cannot support modern GPU cooling needs.
Permit Delays: New facility construction in the West now takes 3-5 years due to regulation.
Power Costs: High electricity prices in Europe make AI training economically unsustainable.
Geographic Concentration: 90% of compute is in 3 regions; the world needs localized diversity.

hero.headline: The Journey to the Silicon Savannah
hero.subheadline: Every great project starts with a single insight. Ours was simple: Kenya has the energy, the world has the need for compute.

sections.title: Identifying the Global Compute Gap
sections.body: The story of Kenya AI Compute began in 2024, during a deep analysis of the global energy crisis and its impact on the booming AI sector. We observed a fundamental mismatch: while the developed world was running out of power to feed its growing GPU hunger, countries in East Africa—led by Kenya—were sitting on massive, underutilized renewable and industrial energy resources. The 'lightbulb moment' happened when we realized that instead of selling low-margin electricity to a local grid, we could build high-margin digital export engines. We spent the first 18 months assembling a world-class consortium of technical experts, securing the perfect industrial site in Kenya, and structuring a deal that protects global capital while empowering the local economy. Today, we are moving from vision to physical reality, building the first 1MW hub of what will become a pan-African AI backbone.

sections.title: Milestones of Our Story
items: 2024 Concept: Discovery of the $0.04/kWh energy arbitrage opportunity.
Consortium Build: Recruiting the top 1% of data center and energy experts.
Kenya Site Lock: Securing a multi-acre industrial parcel with direct plant access.
SEZ Approval: Achieving Special Economic Zone status for the project.
